newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers attack some farm subsidies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers attack some farm subsidies.

text.p: A bipartisan group of House lawmakers Wednesday announced they will seek to eliminate tobacco, sugar and peanut subsidies in the 1998 agriculture appropriations.

Representative Charles Schumer, Democrat of New York, said their amendment to the agriculture funding bill would end the non-recourse (guaranteed) loans in the sugar program which cost $1.4 billion a yaer.

Other amendments would eliminate the peanut subsidy and end federally subsidized crop insurance for tobacco. In addition, Rep. Nita Lowey, Democrat of New York, said she wil seek to stop farm subsidies from going to those who earn $100,000 or more in off-farm income.

"Eliminating this (tobacco) subsidy will save at least $34 million and will help get Uncle Sam out of the tobacco growing business for good," Lowey said at a news conference. The peanut program costs consumers $500 million a year in higher peanut prices, she said.
The House is expected to open debate on the agriculture bill later Wednesday with final passage as early as Thursday.
Republican Reps. Dan Miller of Florida and Steve Chabot of Ohio joined in the oppsiton to the subsidies.
